Compute Prediction Accuracy Metrics

Source: R/tune_imp.R
compute_metrics.Rd

Computes accuracy metrics for each parameter set and repetition in the output of tune_imp().

Usage

compute_metrics(results, metrics = c("mae", "rmse"))

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
compute_metrics(results, metrics = c("mae", "rmse"))

# S3 method for class 'slideimp_tune'
compute_metrics(results, metrics = c("mae", "rmse"))

Arguments

results

A slideimp_tune object or a data frame. The output of tune_imp(), or a data frame whose result list-column holds data frames with truth and estimate columns.

metrics

Character. The metrics to compute, any of "mae", "rmse", "mape", "bias", "rsq", and "rsq_trad". Defaults to c("mae", "rmse").

Value

A data frame with one row per row of results and metric. It keeps every column of results except result, and adds n, the number of masked values, n_miss, the number of those with no estimate, .metric, .estimator, and .estimate.

Details

Each metric is taken over the masked values of one row of results. A masked value with no estimate is left out, and n_miss counts it.

  • "mae": mean absolute error.

  • "rmse": root mean squared error.

  • "mape": mean absolute percentage error, in percent. It divides by the true value, so it is not finite (Inf or NaN) for a repetition in which a masked value is exactly 0. Use another metric for data that contain zeros.

  • "bias": mean of the estimate minus the true value.

  • "rsq": squared Pearson correlation of the estimates and the true values. It is NA when either is constant or fewer than two values have an estimate.

  • "rsq_trad": one minus the residual sum of squares over the total sum of squares. It is NA when the true values are constant or fewer than two values have an estimate.

Examples

set.seed(1234)
obj <- sim_mat(20, 30)$input

results <- tune_imp(
  obj = obj,
  parameters = data.frame(k = 5),
  .f = "knn_imp",
  n_reps = 1,
  num_na = 10,
  .progress = FALSE
)
#> Tuning `knn_imp()`
#> Step 1/2: Resolving NA locations
#> Running mode: sequential
#> Step 2/2: Tuning

compute_metrics(results)
#>   k param_set rep_id error  n n_miss .metric .estimator .estimate
#> 1 5         1      1  <NA> 10      0     mae   standard 0.1074189
#> 2 5         1      1  <NA> 10      0    rmse   standard 0.1302340
